subject: Production: spike in 504s and latency — possible batching/cache issue
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@atlasretail.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena.soto@atlasretail.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:12:03 -0700
Subject: Production: sudden surge in 504s and 429s

Hi Monica —

We started seeing a significant uptick in 504s and 429s hitting our checkout path around 07:50 PST. Error rates jumped from ~0.3% to ~8% and end-to-end latency for some requests is 10–15s. This is causing timeouts in our payment flow.

We temporarily halted non-critical background traffic but customer-facing requests are still failing (we rely heavily on Redwood for text completion embeddings to verify fraud checks). Can someone on your side look now? We can provide logs; attaching a short snippet.

Attachments: atlas_logs_20270419.gz (log bundle, 7MB)

Thanks — Samira
Samira Khan
Ops Lead, AtlasRetail
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:25:41 -0700
Subject: Re: Production: sudden surge in 504s and 429s

Samira — thanks for the alert and logs. We see the initial spike in our telemetry as well (elevated 504/429 and queue depth on the inference workers).

Immediate asks:
- Rishi, can you triage KV-cache / batching layers (priority: determine if cache eviction or batch coalescing is causing queue backlog)?
- Atlas: can you temporarily switch the routing policy to the lower-capacity fallback model (redwood-medium) for the checkout route while we triage? That will reduce token cost but should lower tail latency.
- Please keep logs coming; Samira, if you can capture a single request id that experienced the 15s latency that helps.

Markus and Laura — FYI, customer-visible outage impacting payment flow; raising for exec visibility.

I'll coordinate and keep you updated every hour until resolved.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:03:22 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden surge in 504s and 429s

Quick triage notes (initial pass):
- Observed sustained queue depth growth on the shard serving AtlasRetail's checkout route starting ~07:48. Throughput nominal but worker latency tail increased.
- KV-cache miss rate spiked concurrently with many small, high-concurrency requests (fraud checks). There are signs of cache thrash (high eviction + immediate misses).
- Batching statistics show an abnormal number of very small batches that timed out waiting for coalescing, which then retry and amplify queueing (retry amplification).

Immediate mitigations I recommend (we can push now):
1) Force route to redwood-medium fallback (Monica/Atlas) — reduces per-request compute and bypasses some quantized kernels.
2) Temporarily disable prefix KV-cache for the checkout route (turn caching to pass-through) to stop eviction thrash.
3) Put a conservative per-route batching timeout (from 30ms -> 5ms) to avoid long waits for coalescence causing tail spikes.

Samira: if you confirm you've routed to redwood-medium, we'll push #2 and #3 from our side and monitor. Attaching a debug trace request if you want to upload more samples: debug-trace-20270419.zip.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@atlasretail.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:45:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden surge in 504s and 429s

Rishi / Monica —
We routed the checkout path to redwood-medium at 09:32 and confirmed lower CPU on their side but errors persisted until ~09:40. Attached is one request id that hit the 14.8s tail and the atlas_logs bundle.

Request-id: atlas-req-20270419-7f4b
Attachments: atlas_logs_20270419.gz, debug-trace-20270419.zip

We appreciate the quick help.

—Samira
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 12:15:07 -07:00
Subject: AtlasRetail incident — exec summary and next steps

Laura / Markus — quick exec note for visibility:
- Impact: AtlasRetail production checkout saw elevated 504/429 beginning 07:48 PST. Peak error rate ~8% for 32 minutes; significant revenue impact (estimated).
- Root cause (preliminary): interaction between batching coalescer and KV-cache eviction under a workload of many concurrent small requests caused long coalescing waits and retry amplification (result -> queue backlog and 504s).
- Mitigation applied: route changed to redwood-medium (reduced compute), prefix KV-cache disabled for route, batching timeout lowered. Hotfix rolled to add guard on batch coalescer to avoid indefinite waits.
- Customer asks: incident credit, postmortem, and assurance on config guardrails.

I recommend we:
1) Prepare an official incident postmortem with timeline and remediation (Rishi to lead technical write-up).
2) Offer AtlasRetail a billing credit and a 30-day priority support window as goodwill (sales to propose amount).
3) Add a test case to our regression suite covering high-concurrency small-request patterns to catch coalescer+cache interactions.

Will loop in finance/sales for the credit approval if you agree.

—Monica
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@atlasretail.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 16:03:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: AtlasRetail incident — preliminary RCA and next steps

Final update (preliminary RCA):
- Root cause: an edge case in the batch coalescer where a batch waiter could be left active if a concurrent KV-cache eviction event adjusted the scheduling window. In heavy small-request workloads this produced many tiny batches that timed out; retries from clients and internal backpressure produced queue amplification and 504s.
- What we deployed: a hotfix that introduces a short absolute max coalescence wait and a lightweight per-key eviction backoff that prevents immediate re-insert thrash. Also restored a conservative cache TTL for the checkout route.
- Metrics after fixes: error rate down to baseline ~0.4% within 18 minutes of mitigation; tail latency median improved to sub-200ms for the checkout path.

Next steps (owners):
- Rishi: full technical postmortem + timeline (JIRA: INFRA-6218) and automated regression added to CI.
- Monica/Laura: finalize incident communication and propose a goodwill credit (sales/finance).
- Markus: review runtime knobs for batching defaults and add a canary test in dedicated.

Samira — we'll send the postmortem and a short remediation plan by EOD tomorrow. Appreciate your partnership and apologies for the outage.

Attachments: runbook-fallback-steps.md

—Rishi
SRE, Redwood Inference
